newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac has no plans for reshuffle, election - source.
newsitem.headline: Chirac has no plans for reshuffle, election - source.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac has no plans to make an imminent cabinet reshuffle or call early parliamentary elections, official sources at his office said on Wednesday.
The rumours are "without foundation...all of this is absolutely not on the agenda," a source said.
"The president has time on his hands for reflection," the source said without elaborating.

The statement came after days of rumours that Chirac could bring forward the general election scheduled for March next year or that Prime Minister Alain Juppe might reshuffle his cabinet to streamline the government ahead of the election campaign.

The rumours increased after Gaullist Juppe held unscheduled talks on Wednesday with former defence minister Francois Leotard, the head of the centrist Union for French Democracy (UDF), junior partner of the ruling coalition.
Earlier, Juppe declined to discuss the rumours, merely telling reporters after an unusually brief weekly cabinet meeting: "Oh no, I cannot comment."
